title: Low-Cost Portable ECG Monitor
problem: In many parts of the world, clinical-grade ECG machines are expensive and bulky, limiting cardiac screening in primary-care and rural settings.
targetUsers: Primary-care clinics, community health workers, and students learning biopotential acquisition.
proposedSolution: Build a 3-lead ECG front-end using an instrumentation amplifier and the AD8232 analog front-end, digitize with a microcontroller ADC, apply a digital notch and band-pass filter, and display the waveform with heart-rate detection on a small screen or companion app.
researchDirection: Investigate motion-artifact suppression and adaptive filtering so the device stays accurate during ambulatory use.
futureImprovements: Cloud sync for remote cardiologist review

title: Smart Syringe Infusion Pump
problem: Manual drug infusion is error-prone, and commercial infusion pumps are costly, making precise low-flow delivery hard to access for teaching and low-resource care.
targetUsers: Biomedical engineering labs, teaching hospitals, and researchers requiring controlled micro-dosing.
proposedSolution: Design a stepper-motor-driven syringe pump with closed-loop flow control, a configurable dosing UI, occlusion detection via a load or pressure sensor, and audible/visual alarms following IEC 60601 safety principles.
researchDirection: Study dosing accuracy and occlusion-alarm latency across flow rates to characterise safety margins.

title: Digital Stethoscope with Heart-Sound Recording
problem: Traditional stethoscopes cannot record or share auscultation findings, which limits teaching, telemedicine, and second opinions.
targetUsers: Medical students, telehealth providers, and clinicians in remote areas.
proposedSolution: Capture heart and lung sounds with a microphone in an acoustic chamber, amplify and band-pass filter the signal, digitize it, and store/visualise phonocardiogram waveforms with playback and export for remote review.
researchDirection: Explore automatic murmur detection from phonocardiogram spectral features.

title: Open-Source Pulse Oximeter
problem: Reliable SpO2 measurement became critical during respiratory outbreaks, yet affordable, transparent, and educational devices are scarce.
targetUsers: Students learning photoplethysmography and clinics needing low-cost screening tools.
proposedSolution: Use the MAX30102 optical sensor to acquire red and infrared PPG signals, compute the ratio-of-ratios for SpO2 and derive heart rate, then display readings with basic signal-quality indication.
researchDirection: Investigate calibration against reference oximeters and accuracy across skin tones and perfusion states.

title: Pneumonia Detection from Chest X-Rays
problem: Radiologist shortages delay diagnosis of pneumonia, especially where imaging expertise is limited.
targetUsers: Radiology triage teams and researchers building diagnostic decision-support tools.
proposedSolution: Train a convolutional neural network (transfer learning from ResNet/DenseNet) on public chest-X-ray datasets to classify normal vs. pneumonia, with Grad-CAM heatmaps for explainability.
researchDirection: Address dataset bias and generalisation across scanners and populations, and quantify uncertainty.
futureImprovements: Deployment as a lightweight edge model

title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening from Fundus Images
problem: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of preventable blindness, but screening capacity lags behind the growing diabetic population worldwide.
targetUsers: Ophthalmology screening programs and community health initiatives.
proposedSolution: Build a deep-learning pipeline that grades retinopathy severity from fundus photographs, using image augmentation, class-balancing, and explainable lesion localisation.
researchDirection: Investigate robustness to image-quality variation from low-cost smartphone-based fundus cameras.

title: Clinical Note Summarization with NLP
problem: Clinicians spend excessive time reading and writing lengthy clinical notes, contributing to burnout and documentation errors.
targetUsers: Hospital informatics teams and clinicians managing large caseloads.
proposedSolution: Use transformer-based language models to extract key findings and generate concise summaries from de-identified clinical text, with entity recognition for medications, diagnoses, and follow-ups.
researchDirection: Study factual consistency and hallucination control in medical text generation.

title: Early Sepsis Warning from Vital-Sign Trends
problem: Sepsis progresses rapidly and is often detected too late, dramatically increasing mortality.
targetUsers: Intensive-care units and clinical-decision-support researchers.
proposedSolution: Develop a time-series model (LSTM/temporal transformer) trained on public ICU datasets to predict sepsis onset hours in advance from continuous vitals and labs, optimising for early sensitivity.
researchDirection: Balance early-warning lead time against false-alarm fatigue, and validate across hospitals.

title: IoT Smart Bed Occupancy & Vitals Hub
problem: Nurses cannot continuously watch every patient, so falls and deterioration between rounds go unnoticed.
targetUsers: Hospital wards, elderly-care facilities, and remote-monitoring services.
proposedSolution: Instrument a bed with load sensors and connect wireless vital-sign sensors to an edge gateway that streams data over MQTT to a dashboard, raising alerts for bed-exit events and out-of-range vitals.
researchDirection: Examine edge-vs-cloud processing trade-offs for latency and privacy in continuous monitoring.

title: IoT Vaccine Cold-Chain Monitor
problem: Vaccines and biologics lose potency when temperature excursions in the cold chain go undetected during storage and transport.
targetUsers: Vaccine distribution programs, pharmacies, and public-health logistics teams.
proposedSolution: Deploy connected temperature and humidity loggers that transmit readings to a cloud dashboard, timestamp excursions, and send alerts with a tamper-evident audit trail for each cold-storage unit.
researchDirection: Study low-power wide-area networking (LoRaWAN) for long-range rural cold-chain coverage.

title: Connected Medication Adherence Dispenser
problem: Poor medication adherence, especially among older adults with complex regimens, leads to avoidable hospitalisations.
targetUsers: Patients with chronic conditions, caregivers, and home-health providers.
proposedSolution: Build an automated pill dispenser with timed compartments, reminder alarms, and connectivity that logs each dose and notifies caregivers when a dose is missed.
researchDirection: Investigate behavioural nudges and reminder timing that measurably improve adherence.

title: Wearable Fall-Detection Band
problem: Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults, and delayed help worsens outcomes.
targetUsers: Elderly individuals living independently and their caregivers.
proposedSolution: Use a wrist- or waist-worn inertial measurement unit with an accelerometer and gyroscope; run a threshold + machine-learning classifier to distinguish falls from daily activity and trigger an emergency alert.
researchDirection: Minimise false alarms while keeping sensitivity high across varied movement patterns.

title: Wearable Continuous Body-Temperature Patch
problem: Intermittent thermometer checks miss fever onset and trends, which matter for infection monitoring.
targetUsers: Parents monitoring children, post-operative patients, and remote-care programs.
proposedSolution: Design a skin-adhesive patch with a calibrated temperature sensor that samples continuously and streams to a phone app with trend graphs and fever alerts.
researchDirection: Study skin-contact thermal lag and calibration to core-temperature estimates.

title: Wearable Stress & HRV Monitor
problem: Chronic stress is hard to quantify in daily life, limiting timely mental-health interventions.
targetUsers: Individuals tracking wellbeing and researchers studying stress physiology.
proposedSolution: Acquire wrist PPG to derive heart-rate variability, combine with electrodermal activity, and estimate a stress index using validated HRV features with on-device inference.
researchDirection: Validate stress indices against gold-standard cortisol or self-report under controlled protocols.

title: Electrochemical Glucose Biosensor
problem: Frequent fingerstick glucose testing is painful and discourages the monitoring needed to manage diabetes.
targetUsers: People with diabetes and biosensor researchers exploring minimally invasive sensing.
proposedSolution: Fabricate an enzyme-based (glucose oxidase) electrochemical electrode, read the amperometric current with a potentiostat circuit, and convert it to glucose concentration with calibration.
researchDirection: Improve selectivity, drift, and biocompatibility for continuous monitoring.

title: Smartphone Colorimetric Test-Strip Reader
problem: Reading colorimetric urine or saliva strips by eye is subjective and hard to record objectively.
targetUsers: Point-of-care clinics, home-testing users, and diagnostic researchers.
proposedSolution: Use a smartphone camera with controlled lighting to capture test-strip pads, apply color-calibration, and quantify analyte levels via image analysis with logged results.
researchDirection: Study reproducibility across phone cameras and lighting conditions.

title: Breath Acetone Sensor for Metabolic Monitoring
problem: Non-invasive metabolic monitoring is limited, yet breath biomarkers such as acetone correlate with metabolic states.
targetUsers: Metabolic-health researchers and non-invasive diagnostics developers.
proposedSolution: Use a gas-sensitive metal-oxide or MEMS sensor array to detect acetone in breath, compensate for humidity and interferents, and estimate relative concentration with a calibration model.
researchDirection: Correlate breath-acetone readings with reference metabolic measurements and control cross-sensitivity.

title: Autonomous Ward Delivery Robot
problem: Staff spend significant time transporting medications and samples between hospital rooms, reducing time for direct care and increasing exposure risk.
targetUsers: Hospitals and clinics seeking to automate intra-facility logistics.
proposedSolution: Build a mobile robot with SLAM-based navigation and obstacle avoidance to carry secured payloads between nursing stations and rooms, with authenticated pickup.
researchDirection: Study safe human-aware navigation in dynamic, crowded clinical corridors.

title: Sensorised Laparoscopic Surgery Trainer
problem: Surgical trainees need objective feedback on minimally invasive skills, but many box-trainers offer no measurement.
targetUsers: Surgical education programs and skills-lab instructors.
proposedSolution: Instrument a laparoscopic box-trainer with motion and force sensors to score instrument path length, economy of motion, and applied force, presenting metrics on a dashboard.
researchDirection: Correlate objective metrics with expert-rated surgical proficiency.

title: Low-Cost Teleoperated Assistance Arm
problem: Remote or contamination-sensitive tasks (e.g., handling infectious samples) benefit from teleoperation, but research platforms are costly.
targetUsers: Labs and researchers exploring teleoperation and human-robot interaction.
proposedSolution: Build a leader-follower robotic arm with position/force mapping, latency compensation, and a simple graphical operator interface for remote manipulation of objects.
researchDirection: Investigate haptic feedback and latency compensation for stable teleoperation.

title: Membrane Oxygenator Test Bench
problem: Developing and validating artificial-lung (oxygenator) components requires controlled gas-exchange testing that is hard to access.
targetUsers: Cardiovascular-engineering researchers and artificial-organ developers.
proposedSolution: Build a benchtop circuit with a hollow-fiber membrane module, controlled fluid flow, and inline gas sensors to measure oxygen transfer and pressure drop under varied conditions.
researchDirection: Characterise gas-transfer efficiency vs. hemocompatibility trade-offs in membrane designs.

title: Perfusion Bioreactor for Tissue Scaffolds
problem: Growing engineered tissue requires controlled nutrient perfusion and environmental conditions that static culture cannot provide.
targetUsers: Tissue-engineering and regenerative-medicine research labs.
proposedSolution: Design a sterile perfusion bioreactor that circulates media through a scaffold with regulated flow, temperature, and pH/oxygen monitoring for controlled cell culture.
researchDirection: Study how perfusion parameters affect cell viability and matrix formation within scaffolds.

title: Portable Dialysis Flow Simulator
problem: Wearable and portable artificial-kidney concepts need affordable platforms to prototype and test controlled filtration flow.
targetUsers: Renal-engineering researchers and students studying extracorporeal circuits.
proposedSolution: Construct a benchtop dialysis-flow simulator with regulated dialysate and blood-analog flow across a filter module, measuring pressures and clearance-analog performance.
researchDirection: Explore miniaturisation and sorbent-based dialysate regeneration for wearability.

title: EMG-Controlled Hand Rehabilitation Glove
problem: Stroke and injury survivors need frequent, engaging hand therapy, but clinician time and access are limited.
targetUsers: Rehabilitation clinics and patients recovering hand function at home.
proposedSolution: Build a soft actuated glove that assists finger flexion/extension, triggered by surface-EMG intent detection, with adjustable assistance levels and session logging.
researchDirection: Investigate EMG-driven assist-as-needed control that maximises patient effort and recovery.

title: Instrumented Insole for Gait Analysis
problem: Assessing walking asymmetry and load distribution usually requires expensive lab equipment, limiting routine monitoring.
targetUsers: Physiotherapists, sports scientists, and patients in gait rehabilitation.
proposedSolution: Embed force-sensitive resistors and an IMU in an insole to measure plantar pressure and stride timing, streaming metrics like cadence, symmetry, and stance phases to an app.
researchDirection: Validate insole-derived gait metrics against motion-capture references.

title: VR-Based Upper-Limb Rehabilitation Game
problem: Repetitive rehabilitation exercises are tedious, reducing patient adherence and therapy outcomes.
targetUsers: Neuro-rehabilitation patients and therapists seeking engaging exercise tools.
proposedSolution: Create VR/AR reaching and grasping games that adapt difficulty to patient performance, track range of motion, and export progress reports for clinicians.
researchDirection: Study how adaptive gamification affects motivation and measurable motor recovery.

title: Eye-Gaze Communication Board
problem: People with severe motor impairments (e.g., ALS) may lose the ability to speak or type, needing alternative communication.
targetUsers: Individuals with motor-neuron or spinal conditions and their caregivers.
proposedSolution: Use a webcam and eye-tracking to let users select letters or phrases from an on-screen board, with dwell-based selection and text-to-speech output.
researchDirection: Improve gaze-estimation robustness and reduce calibration burden for daily use.

title: Smart Obstacle-Sensing Cane
problem: White canes detect ground-level obstacles but miss overhead and mid-body hazards for people who are blind or have low vision.
targetUsers: People with visual impairment and orientation-and-mobility trainers.
proposedSolution: Add ultrasonic and time-of-flight distance sensors to a cane that provide haptic vibration feedback proportional to obstacle proximity across multiple heights.
researchDirection: Evaluate feedback encoding schemes that convey obstacle direction and distance intuitively.

title: Real-Time Sign-Language Translator
problem: Communication barriers persist between sign-language users and those who do not sign.
targetUsers: Deaf and hard-of-hearing communities and accessibility service providers.
proposedSolution: Use a camera and a deep-learning model (hand/pose landmarks + sequence model) to recognise sign gestures and convert them to text and speech in real time.
researchDirection: Extend from isolated signs to continuous sign-language sentence recognition across dialects.

title: Brain Tumor Segmentation from MRI
problem: Manual tumor delineation on MRI is slow, subjective, and variable between radiologists.
targetUsers: Neuro-radiology researchers and surgical-planning teams.
proposedSolution: Train a U-Net-style segmentation network on public multimodal brain-MRI datasets to automatically outline tumor regions with volumetric measurement and overlay visualisation.
researchDirection: Improve generalisation across scanners and reduce reliance on large annotated datasets.

title: MRI Reconstruction & Denoising Toolkit
problem: Fast or low-field MRI acquisitions produce noisy, undersampled images that limit diagnostic quality.
targetUsers: Medical-imaging researchers and engineers working on accessible MRI.
proposedSolution: Implement image-reconstruction and denoising algorithms (compressed sensing and deep-learning priors) to recover high-quality images from undersampled k-space data.
researchDirection: Balance reconstruction speed, artifact suppression, and preservation of diagnostic detail.

title: Portable Ultrasound Image Enhancement
problem: Low-cost portable ultrasound images suffer from speckle noise and low contrast, hindering interpretation by non-specialists.
targetUsers: Point-of-care ultrasound users and imaging researchers.
proposedSolution: Develop a processing pipeline that reduces speckle, enhances contrast, and highlights structures in B-mode ultrasound frames, with optional automated measurement tools.
researchDirection: Assess whether enhancement improves measurement reliability without introducing artifacts.

title: Symptom Triage & Health-Literacy Chatbot
problem: People often struggle to decide the urgency of symptoms and where to seek care, leading to delays or unnecessary visits.
targetUsers: Patients seeking guidance and clinics wanting to streamline triage.
proposedSolution: Build a conversational assistant that asks structured triage questions, maps answers to evidence-based urgency guidance, and provides clear next-step recommendations with safety disclaimers.
researchDirection: Study safe design that avoids over-reassurance and clearly escalates emergencies.

title: Lightweight Telemedicine Consultation Platform
problem: Remote and underserved populations lack easy access to specialists, and heavyweight platforms need strong connectivity.
targetUsers: Rural clinics, community health programs, and telehealth providers.
proposedSolution: Develop a secure web app supporting appointment booking, encrypted video consultations, shared vitals/notes, and low-bandwidth fallback modes with privacy safeguards.
researchDirection: Explore low-bandwidth video and store-and-forward workflows for intermittent connectivity.

title: Chronic Disease Self-Management Dashboard
problem: Patients with chronic conditions struggle to track scattered data (glucose, blood pressure, medications) and share it with clinicians.
targetUsers: People managing chronic conditions and their care teams.
proposedSolution: Create an app that aggregates self-reported and device data, visualises trends, sends reminders, and generates shareable clinician-friendly summaries.
researchDirection: Investigate which visualisations and nudges best support behaviour change and self-efficacy.
